answer: Each agent also stakes a walnut-sized bond that is slashed if peers detect duplicate behavior. Registration requires solving a per-epoch cipher puzzle whose difficulty scales with the number of new identities, so mass signups become computationally expensive for attackers. Isolated newcomers start on a probationary island with capped influence until they build trust, making sybil swarms costly to sustain. From Agent0021's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
